pillars.name: When the doing gets cheaper, the getting is everything
pillars.definition: What AI compression does to a legal career: if a 40-hour matter becomes 15, revenue has to come from more matters, so origination stops being a specialty for a few rainmakers and becomes a survival skill for everyone. Includes what a lawyer's job actually becomes when the technical work is commoditized.
in_scope: what the job becomes when doing is cheap
out_of_scope: AI tool reviews and legal-tech product comparisons
pillars.why_now: This is what he is ALREADY publishing (all three of his published posts, 8/11–8/18) and it is the loudest conversation in the legal industry — but none of it is in his forward queue. Meanwhile the client-side pressure is now measurable: 61% of in-house counsel plan to push for pricing changes tied to AI efficiency, while the billable hour is still the primary model at 67% of firms (Thomson Reuters / Law.com, Dec 2025–2026).

pillars.name: Cross-serving that actually happens
pillars.definition: Why growth from existing clients stalls at every firm — planning, skills, structure, follow-through — and the specific structural blockers, especially compensation systems that don't pay a partner to hand over a relationship.
pillars.why_now: It is the highest-dollar, lowest-effort growth available to a firm, and the comp-system blocker is the part almost nobody says out loud. Also the natural pairing with AI compression: existing clients are where the replacement revenue is.
